Czech crude imports from Russia are now zero. The Druzhba pipeline had supplied about half of imports until spring 2025; it stopped in March 2025 (payment problems after US sanctions, state reserves of 330,000 t released to Orlen Unipetrol) and Czechia declared itself independent of Russian oil in April 2025, after the TAL pipeline upgrade raised capacity to 8 Mt a year.

Direct imports of Russian gas were declared zero from 2023 (replaced by Norwegian gas and Dutch and Belgian LNG); Bloomberg found in Nov 2024 that some Russian molecules still reached Czechia indirectly via Slovakia, so the zero is a statement about contracts, not about every molecule.

Russian natural gas stopped on 21 May 2022 when Gasum refused to pay in roubles; before the cutoff Russia covered about 70% of Gasum's requirements. Finland replaced it with the Balticconnector and a floating LNG terminal at Inkoo (operating since 2023), which proved its worth when the Balticconnector was cut in October 2023.

Russian electricity, about a tenth of Finnish consumption, was cut to zero in May 2022 (Fingrid curbed capacity from 1.3 GW to 900 MW in April; the supplier RAO Nordic stopped on 14 May). Olkiluoto 3 (1.6 GW, test production March 2022) replaced a large share of the imports.

Sakhalin-2 LNG supplies about 9% of Japan's LNG imports under contracts running to 2028-2033; Mitsui (12.5%) and Mitsubishi (10%) hold stakes that Tokyo has kept, arguing a break would hand them to Chinese firms; Sakhalin Blend crude is exempt from the G7 price cap for Japan.

Russian natural gas has been banned in Latvia since 1 Jan 2023; the Baltic-Finnish gas market now runs almost entirely on LNG through Klaipeda, Inkoo and Hamina, the last Russian LNG cargo arrived in July 2024, and Russian gas survives only as transit to Kaliningrad through Lithuania.

The Emirate rejects the ICC outright; after the Pre-Trial Chamber issued warrants for the Emir Hibatullah Akhundzada and chief justice Abdul Hakim Haqqani (8 Jul 2025, gender persecution), Mujahid said the Taliban do not recognise any international court nor consider themselves bound by it.
Diplomatic relations established by joint communique on 18 Oct 2020 (Abraham Accords).

On 4 January 2026 Brazil's acting foreign minister, Maria Laura da Rocha, said Brasilia recognises Delcy Rodríguez as head of state in Maduro's absence and opposes any territorial aggression; Lula called the US operation a grave affront to Venezuela's sovereignty and asked the UN for a strong response. This is recognition of a government, not of the state, and the Venezuelan card cites the same reports.
Diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China from 13 November 1975.
Diplomatic relations with the United States from 15 August 1977; the Moroni embassy closed in 1993 and responsibilities moved to Antananarivo in 2006.
Diplomatic relations with Madagascar from 12 November 1976.

Costa Rica and China have had diplomatic relations for 18 years, according to the Chinese foreign ministry's statement of 4 February 2026. The year (2008) is inferred from that count; the 2007 date often given elsewhere is not in any source read here.

Djibouti does not recognise Somaliland: it condemned Israel's recognition of Somaliland (Dec 2025), backs Somalia's territorial integrity, and closed Somaliland's liaison office in Djibouti (Jan 2026).

Dominica recognises the People's Republic of China from the joint communique signed in Beijing on 23 March 2004, moving from the Republic of China (Taiwan). China then offered US$12 million of aid. The Taiwan side is not written here.

Diplomatic relations between Dominica and the United States date from 18 July 1979. Bilateral ties are described as friendly; US aid runs mainly through the World Bank, the CDB and the USAID office in Bridgetown.

Diplomatic relations between Dominica and the United Kingdom date from 3 November 1978, the year of independence from the UK. The UK high commission in Bridgetown covers Dominica; shared agreements include the CARIFORUM-UK EPA, a Tax Information Exchange Agreement and an Investment Agreement.

The FSM recognises the People's Republic of China; diplomatic relations date from 11 September 1989 (FSM mission table). The government marked 20 years of relations in 2009. The Taiwan non-recognition row sits in the datasets, not here.
Diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China since 5 July 1960, according to the Chinese embassy in Accra.
Recognition of the People's Republic of China from 17 March 2016, replacing Taiwan (the 2013 break with Taipei is in the Wikipedia index).

Diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China were established in October 1985, suspended from 1989 and restored in 2005, according to the Chinese embassy in Grenada. The Taiwan side of the switch is not sourced here.

Honduras recognises the People's Republic of China, having shifted recognition from Taipei in 2023 (26 March 2023 per the Taiwan card's sources). Under Asfura the agreements of that switch are under review; no decision by October 2026. Confidence C: the only source read for the recognition itself is Wikipedia (tier 4); the date is taken from the Taiwan card.

Indonesia has no diplomatic relations with Israel; the foreign ministry said in Sept 2025 there would be no recognition or normalisation, through the Abraham Accords or any other platform, unless Israel first recognises an independent Palestinian state.

Israel formally recognised Somaliland as an independent state on 26 Dec 2025 in a joint declaration signed by Netanyahu, Sa'ar and Somaliland's president, the first UN member to do so; Somaliland says it will join the Abraham Accords; Somalia calls the step unlawful.

Tokayev said at the St Petersburg forum on 17 Jun 2022, beside Putin, that Kazakhstan does not recognise the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' ('quasi-state formations'), citing the same principle as for Taiwan, Kosovo, Abkhazia and South Ossetia; the foreign ministry has not recognised the later annexations. Zelensky thanked him. Putin suspended a Kazakh oil shipment via Novorossiysk the next day (reported).

The Supreme Court removed the Taliban from Kazakhstan's list of banned organisations on 20 Dec 2023 (made public by Tokayev on 3 Jun 2024 as a step toward trade and economic cooperation); Astana has not formally recognised the Taliban government, and the foreign ministry cited the absence of the Taliban from the UN terrorist lists.

Kyrgyzstan does not formally recognise the Taliban government, but removed the Taliban from its list of terrorist organisations on 6 Sept 2024 and keeps trade ties with them. The Kremlin said it understood the step.

Recognises the People's Republic of China and broke with Taiwan: the switch was announced on 20 September 2019, and the Chinese foreign ministry records the resumption of relations on 27 September 2019. The Taiwan non-recognition row sits in the datasets, not here.

Full diplomatic relations with the Republic of China (Taiwan) since 23 September 1983 (Wikipedia, 'Diplomatic relations' table). The dataset row from the Taiwan recognition list carries no date; this row adds it and does not replace it.

Kuwait has no relations with Israel and does not recognise it; entry is refused to holders of Israeli passports or Israeli stamps and Israeli goods are boycotted (Wikipedia index). The foreign minister restated on 29 Oct 2023 that Kuwait will not normalise unless a Palestinian state is established in line with international resolutions. Last statement verified in this pass is from October 2023.

No diplomatic relations and no normalisation: the two sides 'do not have formal diplomatic relations'; Aoun and Salam reject 'normalisation', describe peace as a security or non-aggression agreement, and say normalisation would follow the Arab Peace Initiative once the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is resolved. The 26 June 2026 framework's first point affirms each side's right to exist and the intent to end the state of war, so this is a refusal to normalise rather than a denial of Israel's existence; polling cited puts support for normalisation at about 30%.

Full diplomatic relations with the Republic of China (Taiwan), restored 30 April 2007 (the article gives 1 May 2007 in its prose); Saint Lucia had broken with Taiwan for the People's Republic in 1997. The dataset recognition row (since null) is kept; this row dates the current tie.
Diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China established 30 April 1983 by joint communique. The 1990-1994 switch to Taiwan is not written here: the index gives it without citation.
Diplomatic relations with the United Kingdom from 4 October 1966. The 2021 reopening of the British High Commission is the source's case in point.
Does not recognise the PRC: relations, opened on 16 November 1990, are listed as suspended, in the same list that dates the Marshall Islands' recognition of the Republic of China to 20 November 1998.
Mauritius recognises the People's Republic of China; the joint communique establishing diplomatic relations is dated 15 April 1972.

Malaysia has never recognised Israel and has no diplomatic relations; it says it will establish them only after a peace agreement with the State of Palestine. Communications Minister Fahmi (Dec 2023): the port ban signals that Malaysia does not recognise Israel.

Nauru recognises the People's Republic of China again, after severing relations with Taipei on 15 January 2024. The restoration date (24 January 2024) comes from a Wikipedia citation to Reuters (25 January 2024), not opened; the Business Standard source gives the severance.

Oman has not recognised Israel nor opened an embassy, unlike the UAE and Bahrain; it ties normalisation to Palestinian rights (FM Albusaidi, June 2021) and the Consultative Assembly voted in Dec 2022 to widen restrictions on contacts with Israelis. Informal contacts continue.

Pakistan has not recognised Israel since 1948. Foreign Minister Dar said in 2026 there is no change in the policy until a Palestinian state is accepted; in May 2026 Defence Minister Asif rejected Trump's call to join the Abraham Accords as clashing with Pakistan's fundamental ideologies.

Recognised by presidential decree No. 1260 on 26 Aug 2008 (South Ossetia by No. 1261 the same day); embassy-level relations and a joint military base followed. The recognition is the stated reason there is no Russian-Georgian political dialogue.

Russia became the first state to recognise the Taliban government on 3 Jul 2025, after removing the movement from its list of banned organisations; Kabul was then given 'recognised member' status in the Moscow Format.

Saudi Arabia does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations; since Feb 2024 the line is a Palestinian state on the 1967 lines first, repeated by the foreign minister in July 2025. CSIS (July 2026) finds normalisation off the table near term after the Iran war raised the cost of proximity to Israel.

Brussels 'Agreement on the path to normalisation' (27 Feb 2023) and Ohrid implementation annex (18 Mar 2023) accepted but unimplemented - no Association of Serb Municipalities, continued lobbying against Kosovo's memberships.

São Tomé recognises the People's Republic of China: it cut ties with Taiwan on 20 December 2016 and resumed relations with Beijing on 26 December 2016. The dates come from Wikipedia's citations; the Reuters and Chinese MFA pages were not opened.

Permanent neutrality recognised by the General Assembly: resolution 50/80 A, adopted without vote on 12 December 1995, recognises and calls on members to respect and support the status and Turkmenistan's territorial integrity; resolution 69/285 (2015) recalls it. The row records recognition of the status, not membership of a bloc.
Tonga recognises the People's Republic of China (2 November 1998) and broke relations with Taiwan that year. The Taiwan non-recognition row sits in the datasets, not here.

Turkey does not recognise the Republic of Cyprus and backs a two-state, 'sovereign equality' settlement; a UN track is open (Guterres in Cyprus 27-29 Jul 2026, leaders' meetings of 26 Aug, 9 Sep and 17 Sep with the Turkish Cypriot leader Erhurman) and Ankara has not rejected the UN proposals but is said to want EU concessions in return.

Holy See and the State of Palestine established formal diplomatic relations in 2015 through a Comprehensive Agreement. Not in the recognition dataset (its Palestine list omits VAT); written here by hand, to be reconciled.

Holy See maintains diplomatic relations with the Republic of China (Taiwan), the only European state to do so per Wikipedia (index); the mission moved to Taipei in 1951. Not in the recognition dataset (its Taiwan list does include VAT, with no date or source); written here by hand.

issues.title: Taiwan
issues.subtitle: who recognises the Republic of China
issues.why: Twelve governments keep formal ties with Taipei; everyone else has chosen Beijing. The list shrinks every few years.

issues.title: Palestine
issues.subtitle: who recognises the State of Palestine
issues.why: The 2024-25 wave of Western recognitions moved the line that had stood since 1988.

issues.title: Kosovo
issues.subtitle: who recognises it
issues.why: Recognition is Serbia's and Kosovo's whole contest; five EU members still refuse, Belgrade campaigns for withdrawals.

issues.title: Ukraine
issues.subtitle: the last General Assembly vote on the war
issues.why: The February 2026 vote, with the United States abstaining, shows where the coalition stands four years in.

issues.title: Ukraine, March 2022
issues.subtitle: the first vote on the aggression
issues.why: The baseline - 141 in favour - against which every later vote on Ukraine is read.

issues.title: Annexations
issues.subtitle: the October 2022 vote on Russia's annexation of Ukrainian regions
issues.why: Territorial integrity is the one principle almost every state will vote for, even those close to Moscow.

issues.title: Srebrenica
issues.subtitle: the 2024 genocide remembrance vote
issues.why: Serbia campaigned against it and counted the 68 abstentions as a victory; the vote maps the Balkans' memory wars onto the world.

issues.title: Gaza
issues.subtitle: the 2024 vote to end Israel's presence in the territories
issues.why: The clearest line of the Gaza war in the Assembly, with the West split in three.

issues.title: Palestine at the UN
issues.subtitle: the September 2026 vote on Palestine's participation
issues.why: After the recognitions, the procedural vote that measures them.
